title: Find Missing Number
question: Find the one missing integer from an array containing distinct values from 0 through n.
answer: The expected sum is n(n+1)/2; subtract the actual sum to obtain the missing value in linear time and constant extra space. In JavaScript ensure the sums remain within safe integer precision or use BigInt throughout. XOR is another linear method but ordinary bitwise operators coerce to signed 32-bit integers, so it is not a universal numeric replacement.
followUp: Reject duplicates/out-of-range values in a validation variant and explain the extra work needed to verify the precondition.

title: Max SubArray
question: Return the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous subarray, including all-negative inputs.
answer: Maintain the best sum ending at the current element and the best sum seen anywhere. At each value choose between starting a new segment there and extending the previous segment. Initialize from the first element rather than zero, otherwise an all-negative array incorrectly returns an empty segment’s sum. This is O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary state.
followUp: Return segment indices and define a deterministic tie-breaker between equally good segments.

title: Make Counter
question: Create independent closure-based counters with increment, decrement, and reset operations.
answer: Capture the current count and initial value inside a factory invocation. Return methods that update that private binding; each factory call receives its own environment. State whether methods return the new value or the previous one and keep the API consistent. A closure encapsulates state from ordinary callers but does not create persistence or shared server coordination.
followUp: Add a bounded variant that reports rejected transitions without letting count and error state diverge.

title: Power of Two
question: Determine whether a positive integer is an exact power of two without misclassifying non-integers.
answer: For a safe-integer Number, reject nonpositive or noninteger values and divide by two while the remainder is zero; accept exactly when the final value is one. This takes O(log n) time and avoids the 32-bit coercion of n & (n-1). A BigInt implementation can use that bit identity safely for arbitrary-width positive integers.
followUp: Implement Number and BigInt variants with separate input contracts rather than mixing numeric types.

title: sum()
question: Implement a curried accumulator whose chain is explicitly terminated by an empty call.
answer: Return a function that captures the current total. A numeric argument produces another accumulator and an empty call returns the total. This avoids surprising implicit coercion through valueOf or toString. Define whether each call accepts one value or a batch and reject unsupported values. Use immutable closure state when chains must be safely reusable.
followUp: Support grouped arguments while keeping termination unambiguous and avoiding mutation shared by sibling chains.

title: Password Strength
question: Build password feedback that recomputes independent checks after every edit, including deletion.
answer: Keep only the password string in state and derive the check results while rendering. Treat empty input separately from a failed policy. Use a labelled password input and a live feedback region, and never persist or log the secret. A checklist measures compliance with the chosen rules, not entropy or resistance to credential attacks.
followUp: Add a policy configuration and explain how server validation remains authoritative.

title: URL Validator
question: Inspect a website address without navigating to it. Accept an explicit HTTP(S) scheme and reject embedded credentials.
answer: Trim for validation, parse with URL inside try/catch, then apply a separate protocol and credential policy. Derive normalized output and feedback from the same input so invalid edits clear stale results. A valid URL is not necessarily safe for a server to fetch: destination restrictions and redirect handling belong on that server.
followUp: Add a domain allowlist and discuss DNS resolution and redirect checks separately from browser syntax validation.

title: Get Result By Path
question: Read an own-property path from nested JSON-like data without evaluating code or traversing prototypes.
answer: Prefer a path-segment array for an unambiguous contract. Walk one segment at a time, verify the current value can hold properties, and use Object.hasOwn before indexing. Return a documented fallback for a missing segment while distinguishing a present undefined value if required. Dot/bracket string parsing is a separate grammar; do not use eval to implement it.
followUp: Add a string-path parser that supports escaping and explicitly forbids unsafe prototype-related traversal.

title: Find smallest number
question: Return the minimum finite number in a nonempty array without sorting or mutating the input.
answer: Initialize the minimum from the first accepted value and scan once, replacing it whenever a smaller value appears. This is O(n) time and O(1) extra space, compared with unnecessary O(n log n) sorting. Define empty and invalid-value behavior explicitly. Avoid spreading a very large array into Math.min, which can exceed function argument limits.
followUp: Return both minimum value and first index with a deterministic tie rule.

title: Chips Input
question: Create a keyboard-driven tag editor with trimmed labels, case-insensitive uniqueness, removal, and a configurable capacity.
answer: Model draft, ordered tags, and feedback separately. On Enter normalize the draft, reject blanks, detect duplicates before capacity, and add immutably. Preserve display capitalization while comparing a normalized key. Remove by stable identity and support Backspace only on an empty draft; ignore command keys during IME composition in a production version.
followUp: Support pasted delimiters without treating a composing IME Enter as a completed tag.

title: Progress Bar
question: Render a determinate completion meter from a numeric prop while keeping text, fill, and accessible values consistent.
answer: Accept finite numbers, clamp into the documented range, and round once. Use the resulting value for every visual and semantic representation instead of copying props into independent state. A progressbar needs an accessible name and numeric bounds. Unknown total work should be represented as indeterminate rather than a fabricated percentage.
followUp: Add an indeterminate mode with no aria-valuenow and respect reduced-motion preferences.

title: Mortgage Calculator
question: Create an educational monthly-payment estimator with explicit invalid-input and zero-interest behavior.
answer: Keep raw field strings until submission, reject blanks before numeric conversion, and validate finite values and the allowed term. Convert the annual percentage rate to a monthly decimal rate. Use principal divided by months at zero interest and the amortization formula otherwise. Clear a previous result when validation fails; format only the final amount.
followUp: Explain how lender-specific schedules, decimal arithmetic, fees, and rounding change a production calculation.

title: Power of Three
question: Check whether a positive integer is a power of three using exact integer operations.
answer: Validate a positive integer, repeatedly divide by three while divisible, and accept only if the remainder value becomes one. Floating-point logarithm comparisons can be close to an integer without being exact and need additional proof or checks. Safe-integer limits still apply to Number input; use a separate BigInt contract for arbitrary-size integers.
followUp: Find the exponent as well as the boolean result without relying on floating-point logarithms.

title: Accordion
question: Build a single-open answer list whose buttons and visible panels expose matching accessibility relationships.
answer: A single open item ID or null encodes the invariant that at most one panel is expanded. Use native buttons, stable IDs, aria-expanded, and labelled regions. Derive both rendering and attributes from that ID. Decide explicitly whether closed panels unmount or remain hidden, since nested form state and focus behavior differ.
followUp: Preserve nested panel input state while keeping hidden controls out of the keyboard order.

title: Dark Mode
question: Create an appearance switch scoped to one embedded surface rather than modifying the host document.
answer: Initialize a boolean once from the supported initial preference, toggle with a functional updater, and derive surface colors, text, and aria-pressed from that same value. Theme state belongs to the surface in this exercise. An application-wide theme instead needs a shared preference owner and a deliberate server-rendered initial value.
followUp: Extend to system appearance while keeping an explicit user choice higher priority.

title: Count Negative
question: Count strictly negative numeric entries while distinguishing negative zero from values below zero.
answer: Scan once and increment the count only when the value is less than zero under a documented finite-number input contract. JavaScript negative zero is not less than zero and should not be counted as a negative amount under this definition. If invalid entries are possible, decide whether to reject the array or skip them rather than relying on coercion.
followUp: Return counts for negative, zero, and positive buckets in one pass.

title: Find largest number
question: Find the maximum finite value in a numeric sequence and state the empty-input contract.
answer: Use a single pass with an initial value taken from the sequence rather than zero, which fails for all-negative data. Keep validation separate from comparison and avoid sorting solely to obtain an extremum. For streaming input, maintain the same accumulator incrementally. Time is O(n) and auxiliary space is O(1).
followUp: Compute minimum and maximum together and report their stable first positions.

title: Loop A to Z
question: Generate the uppercase ASCII alphabet as a sequence without hard-coding every letter.
answer: Iterate over the integer code points from A through Z and convert each with String.fromCharCode or String.fromCodePoint. This works because the chosen ASCII letters form a contiguous range. It is not a general method for producing every locale’s alphabet; scripts, digraphs, and collation orders need a different model.
followUp: Parameterize the range and reject surrogate or invalid Unicode code points deliberately.

title: Custom Sort
question: Sort records by priority, then by a stable secondary key, without changing the input array.
answer: Copy the array and use a comparator that compares priority numerically before applying the chosen secondary comparison. Return zero for a true tie and add an ID tie-breaker when deterministic total ordering is needed. The comparator must be consistent and transitive; it must not mutate records or use changing random values.
followUp: Accept a list of sort descriptors and define explicit null placement and locale behavior.

title: implement curry()
question: Transform a fixed-arity function into a reusable argument-collecting function.
answer: Capture collected arguments in a new closure for each call, and invoke the original once the declared arity is satisfied. Preserve the receiver according to an explicit policy, commonly the receiver of the final invocation. Function.length is only a default hint because optional and rest parameters change its meaning. An explicit arity makes the contract clearer.
followUp: Add placeholders and explain how filling argument holes changes the collection algorithm.

title: once(fn)
question: Wrap a function so only its first successful evaluation is cached and reused.
answer: Store a hasResult flag separately from the cached value so undefined, zero, and false can still be valid results. Invoke with apply to preserve the receiver. Decide whether a thrown error consumes the once opportunity; for this contract it does not. Async rejection requires another explicit policy because caching a promise shares both its pending result and rejection.
followUp: Create an async once variant and choose whether rejected work is cached or retried.

title: groupBy(arr, key)
question: Group records by a selected key while preserving input order within each bucket.
answer: Use a Map when keys may be objects or when arbitrary string keys must not collide with object prototypes. Scan once, create a bucket on the first occurrence, and append without mutating source records. Time is O(n) plus output storage. If returning a plain object is required, define key conversion and use a null-prototype object safely.
followUp: Accept a key-selector function and compare Map identity semantics with serialized compound keys.

title: Filter Recipes
question: Filter kitchen cards by a name query and category while retaining selected recipe IDs when rows are hidden.
answer: Store the query, category, and selected IDs; derive visible rows from immutable recipe props. Combine a trimmed case-insensitive name match with the exact category predicate. Keep selection independent of filtering so changing a view cannot delete a user decision. Generate category options once per dataset change in a documented order.
followUp: Define how a refreshed dataset distinguishes a hidden recipe from a deleted or unavailable selection.

title: Remove Duplicates from Array
question: Remove repeated primitive values while preserving the order of first occurrence.
answer: Track seen values with a Set and append only the first encounter. Set uses SameValueZero semantics, so NaN values deduplicate and positive/negative zero share an identity. Object entries are compared by reference, not structural content. State that behavior instead of presenting a primitive deduplicator as deep equality.
followUp: Deduplicate objects by a supplied stable ID and define first-wins versus last-wins behavior.

title: Voting Eligibility
question: Implement a configurable minimum-age predicate without embedding legal assumptions in code.
answer: Accept a validated integer age and a caller-supplied minimum age, then compare them directly. Reject invalid or negative ages according to the contract; do not use truthiness because zero is a valid numeric value. The exercise is a threshold model, not a complete jurisdictional eligibility determination, which may depend on additional current rules and verified identity.
followUp: Accept a birth date and calculate completed calendar years before applying the supplied threshold.

title: Validate Palindrome
question: Check whether text is a palindrome under an explicit case and character-normalization policy.
answer: Normalize the string according to the contract, then compare characters from both ends while moving inward. A two-pointer check is O(n) time and can avoid constructing a reversed copy after normalization. Specify whether punctuation, accents, and spaces are ignored. For code-point or grapheme semantics, tokenize before indexing rather than assuming UTF-16 units are characters.
followUp: Compare a strict literal palindrome checker with a locale-aware user-text variant.

title: Implement a Stack
question: Implement a last-in-first-out stack with push, pop, peek, and size.
answer: Keep the backing array private and expose operations with documented empty behavior. Array push/pop provide amortized O(1) operations at the end; unshift/shift needlessly move entries. Return size from actual storage rather than maintaining an inconsistent second counter. If undefined can be a valid value, use an explicit result shape or size check to distinguish underflow.
followUp: Add a minimum-value operation using an auxiliary minimum stack with duplicate minima handled correctly.

title: Power of Four
question: Identify positive integers that are exact powers of four without relying on 32-bit masks.
answer: Repeatedly divide a validated positive integer by four while divisible and accept only when the final value is one. An alternative is to identify a power of two and verify an even exponent, but bit masks in ordinary Number operators are restricted to 32-bit coercion. Define a separate BigInt version if wider integer support is needed.
followUp: Return the base-four exponent and test values beyond the signed 32-bit range.

title: Count even numbers
question: Count even integers in an array while rejecting unsupported numeric values.
answer: For a validated integer array, scan once and count values whose remainder modulo two is zero. Zero and negative even integers qualify. Non-integers and unsafe integers require a documented validation policy because parity of an already-rounded Number may not match the original value. The algorithm is O(n) with constant auxiliary space.
followUp: Partition the input into even and odd collections while retaining original order.

title: Back To Top
question: Show a return-to-top control only after the reader passes a configured scroll threshold.
answer: Subscribe to scrolling once, use a passive listener, and coalesce measurement with requestAnimationFrame if needed. Track only whether the threshold is crossed instead of rerendering for every pixel. Use a native button with a descriptive name and choose instant scrolling when reduced motion is requested. Remove the listener and cancel pending work on unmount.
followUp: Make the threshold relative to a scrollable container rather than the browser window.

title: Copy to Clipboard
question: Copy a user-edited snippet and report success only after the clipboard operation succeeds.
answer: Invoke clipboard writing from a user gesture and await its promise. Treat unsupported or rejected access as a real failure, with a selectable-text or legacy copy fallback where appropriate. Keep copied feedback separate from the input, clear its timer on unmount, and avoid announcing success before permission or browser restrictions are known.
followUp: Add a copyable code block whose feedback resets when its source changes.

title: Capitalize Words
question: Capitalize the first character of each whitespace-delimited word under a specified locale policy.
answer: Choose whether the rest of each word is preserved or lowercased, then implement exactly that rule. Tokenization and reconstruction determine whether original spacing is retained. Uppercasing can expand a character into multiple code points, so do not assume a fixed output length. Treat this as formatting, not a general person-name normalization algorithm.
followUp: Preserve whitespace exactly using token-aware replacement rather than split-and-join.

title: Count Vowels
question: Count ASCII vowel occurrences case-insensitively and make the scope explicit.
answer: Scan characters once and test membership in a small vowel set after case normalization. Count occurrences, not distinct vowels. State that the exercise uses a/e/i/o/u and does not automatically model accented vowels or the linguistic role of y. A broader language-aware version needs a chosen normalization and alphabet policy.
checks: accented letters under the declared policy.
followUp: Return counts per vowel and compare Unicode decomposition with a language-specific definition.

title: Contact Form
question: Build a contact form with visible labels, field-specific validation, and a guarded asynchronous submit state.
answer: Keep raw fields in state and validate on a documented boundary such as blur or submit. Derive field errors from the current values, connect them with aria-describedby, and move focus to the first invalid field on submit. Prevent duplicate requests while pending. Keep client validation distinct from server validation and preserve typed input after a server failure.
followUp: Add server field errors without erasing newer edits made while a request was in flight.

title: Sum of all numbers in an array
question: Sum finite numeric entries using an explicit zero result for an empty array.
answer: Use a linear accumulator or reduce with an initial zero so empty input is defined. Reject or explicitly handle NaN and infinities rather than allowing one invalid value to silently poison the total. Ordinary floating-point addition is order-sensitive; currency, huge integers, and high-accuracy measurements may require different representations or summation algorithms.
followUp: Implement compensated summation and compare it with integer-minor-unit arithmetic for money.

title: Array to Zigzag String Converter
question: Convert a word list into alternating forward/reversed words, leaving the input array untouched.
answer: First define what zigzag means: here even-indexed words remain unchanged and odd-indexed words reverse by Unicode code points; join with one space. Use map for a pure transformation and Array.from for code-point reversal. This contract intentionally differs from a matrix zigzag traversal. A UI should parse input and render the derived output without a second synchronized state variable.
followUp: Extend reversal to user-perceived graphemes and state the required segmentation support.

title: Auto Save Text
question: Auto-save a draft after an idle period and display saved, saving, and error states.
answer: Keep the editable draft separate from the last acknowledged revision. Debounce writes with effect cleanup, and attach a revision to each save so a late response cannot mark newer text saved. Local storage writes can throw and remote writes can arrive out of order. Report saved only for the current acknowledged draft; do not equate a queued request with durable storage.
followUp: Retry failed saves and reconcile an external edit without silently overwriting either draft.

title: Counter Using React
question: Create a bounded quantity counter with increment, decrement, and reset actions.
answer: Represent the count in one state value and use functional updaters when the next value depends on the previous one. Clamp transitions at the documented bounds and disable controls whose action is unavailable. Reset to the initial configured count rather than an accidental hard-coded value. Prefer derived disabled states over additional booleans.
followUp: Support a changed step size without allowing updates to escape the valid range.

title: Anagram Checker
question: Check whether two strings have the same character multiplicities under a chosen normalization rule.
answer: Normalize both strings consistently and compare frequency maps, decrementing counts as the second string is scanned. Reject a length mismatch after normalization. This is linear in text length, with space proportional to the alphabet encountered. Sorting is simpler in some contexts but usually costs O(n log n). Clarify code-point versus grapheme semantics.
followUp: Compare normalized canonical equivalents without accidentally discarding meaningful language distinctions.

title: findMaxNumber
question: Return the largest value and its first occurrence in a stream of finite numbers.
answer: Maintain the best value and index while scanning, replacing them only on a strict greater-than comparison to preserve the first tie. Initialize only after a first valid item; an empty stream needs a separate result. This extends the maximum-value exercise with a stable witness and works incrementally without storing the full stream.
followUp: Adapt the accumulator to an async iterable and propagate cancellation and source failures.

title: Factorial of a number
question: Compute factorial for a nonnegative integer using a representation that preserves the requested range.
answer: Define 0! as one, validate an integer input, and multiply iteratively from two through n. Number quickly loses exact integer precision, so BigInt is appropriate for exact large factorials. Convert factors consistently instead of mixing Number and BigInt multiplication. Avoid recursion solely for this loop, since it adds stack depth without improving the model.
followUp: Return the number of trailing decimal zeros using factors of five rather than constructing the entire factorial.

title: Fibonacci Series
question: Produce the first n Fibonacci values with F0=0 and F1=1.
answer: Validate n as a nonnegative count, then iteratively update a pair of consecutive values and emit the requested count. This is O(n) additions and O(n) output storage; retaining only the nth value needs constant auxiliary storage. A naive recursive implementation repeats work exponentially. Use BigInt when exact values outgrow safe Number precision.
followUp: Compute the nth term with fast doubling in logarithmic recursion depth.

title: Secret Code Shuffler
question: Create a reversible educational character shift over a declared alphabet.
answer: Treat this original exercise as a Caesar-style shift, not encryption: normalize the shift modulo the alphabet size, map only supported letters, and preserve other characters according to the contract. The inverse subtracts the same normalized shift. Negative modulo in JavaScript needs normalization with ((x % m)+m)%m to keep indices nonnegative.
followUp: Distinguish this toy substitution from authenticated encryption and avoid presenting obfuscation as security.

title: Tooltip
question: Show concise supplemental help on both pointer hover and keyboard focus.
answer: Keep the trigger accessible without requiring the tooltip. Use an element with role=tooltip and associate it through aria-describedby. Open on hover or focus, close on Escape and the appropriate pointer/focus exit, and clean up delay timers. A tooltip should not contain interactive controls; use a popover or dialog when users must interact with its content.
followUp: Position the help near viewport edges without clipping or creating an interactive hover trap.

title: Guess the number
question: Build a number-guessing game with a fixed secret per round, finite input validation, and restart.
answer: Create the secret at round initialization rather than on every render. Store guesses and round status; derive high/low/correct feedback from a validated integer. Specify whether invalid guesses consume attempts and enforce that rule consistently. Disable guessing when a round ends and create a new secret only on restart. Inject randomness for deterministic tests.
followUp: Add a reproducible seed and a history view without leaking the secret into normal UI state displays.

title: Toggle button with custom hook
question: Extract reusable boolean state behavior into a useToggle hook without hiding the underlying React lifecycle.
answer: Return the current boolean and stable operations for toggle, set true, and set false. Use a lazy initial value and a functional updater for inversion, so multiple queued toggles compose correctly. Reuse the hook only for identical behavior; it should not own unrelated rendering, network access, or global theme policy.
followUp: Allow a controlled parent mode and define who owns state rather than mixing two authorities.

title: Leap year
question: Create a year inspector using Gregorian leap-year rules and reject non-integer input.
answer: Validate the raw input before coercion, then use the ordered divisibility rule: divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. A century is the important counterexample to the naive divide-by-four shortcut. State the supported year range and calendar; do not silently apply contemporary Gregorian rules to historical calendars.
followUp: Add a calendar selection and explain why a historical date may require jurisdiction-specific rules.

title: Blog Post
question: Render a reusable article component with semantic structure, plain-text content, and an unavailable-image fallback.
answer: Keep article data separate from presentation. Use article, an appropriate heading level, a time element with a machine-readable datetime, and useful image alt text. Render author/content as text unless rich HTML has a separate sanitization policy. Avoid redundant state for props and supply explicit empty or missing-field behavior.
followUp: Support a sanitized rich-content format while keeping heading hierarchy and link semantics intact.

title: Flatten Nested Array
question: Flatten arbitrarily nested arrays while preserving left-to-right leaf order.
answer: Walk each element: recurse or push explicit stack frames for arrays and append non-array leaves. An explicit stack avoids call-stack overflow for deep nesting. Specify hole behavior, depth limits, and whether cyclic arrays are rejected. Keep cycle detection on the active ancestry path if repeated shared arrays should be expanded at each occurrence.
followUp: Support a maximum flattening depth and compare path-cycle detection with global deduplication.

title: Even or odd
question: Create an integer parity inspector that distinguishes invalid input from even and odd values.
answer: Reject blank and non-integer values before applying remainder. An integer is even when its remainder modulo two is zero, including negative even integers. Do not use truthiness to validate zero. If the contract must support values beyond Number safe-integer precision, parse and validate a BigInt input rather than classifying an already-rounded Number.
followUp: Add a BigInt mode and keep its parsing error messages separate from ordinary numeric input.

title: Read More
question: Build an excerpt that expands and collapses without losing the original article content.
answer: Derive the excerpt from immutable full text and store only whether it is expanded. Hide the toggle for content that already fits. Define the truncation unit, such as words, so an arbitrary UTF-16 cut does not split text unexpectedly. Keep the button label and aria-expanded aligned with the same state.
followUp: Preserve a stable focus target and selection when switching between excerpt and full text.

title: Acronym Generator
question: Create initials from a trimmed phrase and define a consistent separator policy.
answer: Normalize leading/trailing whitespace, split on runs of whitespace, discard empty segments, and take the first code point of each remaining token. Uppercase the result with an explicit locale policy if needed. The result is derived from the phrase, not synchronized through an effect. State whether hyphenated words count as one token or multiple words.
followUp: Offer a configurable stop-word list while retaining a clear preview of which words contributed initials.

title: Character Counter
question: Display a live text length and remaining budget using a declared counting unit.
answer: Choose UTF-16 units, code points, or grapheme clusters explicitly because they produce different answers for emoji and combining marks. For a user-facing text budget, grapheme segmentation is often the desired model when supported. Derive count and remaining budget, and decide whether excess input is rejected or merely reported. Keep announcements restrained during typing.
followUp: Support separate user-visible grapheme counts and server byte limits without conflating the two.

title: Dynamic Greeting App
question: Render a greeting from a chosen display name and a deterministic time-of-day policy.
answer: Keep the name editable, trim it for display, and use a fallback for blank names. Pass or inject the current time so tests are deterministic. If the greeting must change over time, own a timer with cleanup; reading the clock once does not create a live clock. Specify the timezone instead of assuming every user shares the server clock.
followUp: Show a user-selected timezone and handle the case where the device time changes.

title: Get Weekday
question: Determine the weekday for a calendar-date input without a timezone-induced off-by-one error.
answer: Treat YYYY-MM-DD as calendar fields rather than blindly parsing a timestamp. Validate that the reconstructed year/month/day matches the requested fields. Either compute consistently in UTC and format in UTC or intentionally use local calendar construction. Do not mix a UTC midnight parse with local weekday formatting.
followUp: Add locale-specific weekday labels while preserving the same calendar date.

title: Focus Input
question: Move focus to an input from a separate action and optionally select its existing value.
answer: Keep a DOM ref with useRef, attach it to the input, and call focus in the event handler. Refs store imperative handles without triggering rendering. Guard against an absent or disabled input, and do not steal focus automatically after every render. If autofocus is a requirement, perform it at a deliberate lifecycle boundary.
followUp: Focus the first invalid input after form submission without fighting a user’s current typing position.

title: Authentication
question: Model a demo sign-in interface with explicit loading, authenticated, anonymous, and error states.
answer: Separate the form from session state. A request can transition anonymous to loading and then authenticated or error; stale responses must not overwrite a newer sign-out or account choice. Client UI state is not authorization. A real protected API validates its session on the server, and secrets or pretend token strings should not be stored as a demonstration of security.
followUp: Keep a public screen usable during background session refresh while preserving account isolation.

title: shuffle()
question: Return an unbiased permutation using Fisher–Yates and an injectable random source.
answer: Copy the input, then for each position from the end choose a uniform integer between zero and that position inclusive and swap. Every permutation is equally likely only if the bounded choices are uniform. Sorting with a random comparator is neither a valid comparator nor an unbiased shuffle. Deterministic tests should inject controlled random outputs.
followUp: Use rejection-sampled cryptographic integers for a stronger randomness requirement and explain why distribution tests are not a proof.

title: Navbar
question: Build a responsive site navigation with a current-page indicator and a keyboard-usable mobile disclosure.
answer: Use nav and ordinary links for page navigation. Use a button for the mobile disclosure, expose aria-expanded and aria-controls, and close it after navigation or Escape. Mark the current page with aria-current rather than relying only on color. Avoid role=menu unless implementing that complete keyboard interaction model.
followUp: Handle focus restoration when a mobile drawer closes after an in-app route change.

title: Largest number formed
question: Arrange nonnegative integer strings so their concatenation is lexicographically/numerically maximal.
answer: Sort strings using the order of a+b versus b+a rather than ordinary numeric value or first digit alone. Concatenations have equal lengths for each pair, so lexicographic comparison is appropriate without converting huge strings to Number. Join the result and normalize an all-zero result to a single zero. State input validity and leading-zero policy.
followUp: Explain why the pairwise concatenation comparator establishes the required ordering and keep arithmetic precision out of the comparison.

title: Color Explorer
question: Create a color preview from validated hexadecimal input and keep invalid drafts editable.
answer: Store the draft independently from the last valid color. Accept a documented form, such as #RRGGBB, and derive a normalized valid value for CSS. Render validation feedback without replacing the user’s incomplete typing. Do not interpolate arbitrary input into a style string. Choose a readable foreground using computed contrast instead of guessing from a color name.
followUp: Support RGB input with an explicit conversion and show contrast against candidate text colors.

title: Confirmation Modal
question: Ask for explicit confirmation before a destructive local action, with focus restored when the dialog closes.
answer: Keep pending intent separate from the confirmed action. Prefer a native dialog opened with showModal so background content becomes inert. Provide a title, clear confirm/cancel names, Escape cancellation, and deliberate initial focus. Commit the action only on confirmation and restore focus to the original trigger after closing.
checks: long content on a small screen.
followUp: Represent asynchronous confirmation with a pending state and prevent accidental duplicate execution.

title: Toggle password
question: Add a show/hide control to a password input without changing its value or submitting the form.
answer: Keep visibility as a boolean independent of the controlled password string. Switch type between password and text, use a button with type=button, and expose a clear Show password or Hide password action. Preserve focus/caret where the browser permits it. Do not duplicate, log, or persist the field merely to implement visibility.
followUp: Support press-and-hold reveal with pointer cancellation while retaining a keyboard-accessible alternative.

title: Array Chunking
question: Split an array into consecutive chunks of a positive integer size without modifying the input.
answer: Validate the size before looping so zero or negative values cannot cause an infinite loop. Iterate start positions by size and slice each segment, allowing the final chunk to be shorter. This is O(n) copied output with O(n) total output storage. An iterator variant can yield chunks incrementally for a large source.
followUp: Implement lazy chunking over an iterable and define whether the final partial chunk is emitted.

title: Tab Switcher
question: Create simple content switching where one active section is selected by a stable key.
answer: Model the active key, derive the visible content, and decide whether inactive content should remain mounted. When using the ARIA tabs pattern, pair tabs and panels and implement expected arrow-key navigation rather than adding roles cosmetically. Ordinary buttons are sufficient for a simpler section-switching contract that does not claim tabs semantics.
followUp: Let URL state select a section and define how browser back/forward changes the active key.

title: usePreviousHook
question: Implement a hook that exposes a value from the previous committed render.
answer: Use a ref to retain the prior value and update it in an effect after commit. During rendering return the existing ref value, which is undefined on the initial render. Do not assign the ref while rendering to pretend the current value is previous. Decide whether equality-based suppression belongs in a separate abstraction.
followUp: Implement previous-distinct-value semantics and explain how it differs from previous-render semantics.

title: Sum of n natural numbers
question: Compute 1+2+…+n for a nonnegative integer and state numeric precision limits.
answer: Use n(n+1)/2 rather than a loop when only the total is required. With BigInt, divide one even factor before or after multiplication using exact integer arithmetic. Number inputs need safe-integer validation for both the input and result; a small enough input type does not automatically guarantee the product remains exactly representable.
followUp: Compute a closed integer range sum and avoid overflow-prone intermediate operations in fixed-width languages.

title: Holy Grail
question: Create a semantic header/sidebar/main/aside/footer layout that collapses into a readable single column.
answer: Use CSS Grid to express the desktop areas and a minmax(0,1fr) content track to allow internal overflow. Preserve a sensible DOM reading order rather than visually rearranging essential content into a confusing tab order. At narrow widths stack the secondary regions or provide intentional disclosures. Avoid fixed content heights that clip long text.
followUp: Make the main region independently scrollable without trapping browser navigation or hiding the footer.

title: User profile
question: Render a profile summary with explicit missing-data, loading, and failure states.
answer: Accept a profile object rather than mixing fetch logic into a presentational card. Show a useful fallback for a missing avatar or optional bio and use meaningful image alternative text. If fetching is required, keep pending/error/success states explicit and ignore stale account responses. Never infer authorization from a displayed profile ID.
followUp: Separate public profile fields from account-private details using a server-defined response contract.

title: Age calculator
question: Compute completed years of age from a valid birthday and an injected current date.
answer: Validate date fields and reject future birthdays. Start with the difference in calendar years, then subtract one when the current month/day is before the birthday. Specify a February-29 birthday policy for non-leap years. Milliseconds divided by a fixed year length are not a reliable calendar-age calculation.
followUp: Show years/months/days with an explicit calendar borrowing policy rather than fixed-duration arithmetic.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
question: Build a searchable help index that preserves which answer the reader deliberately expanded.
answer: Represent FAQ items by stable IDs and derive matches from normalized question/body text. Keep expansion separate from the filtered array, so hiding a row is not mistaken for deleting it. Use native heading buttons and associated answer regions. Specify whether multiple answers may remain expanded, and provide a useful no-results state.
followUp: Group results by category while avoiding duplicate IDs in accessibility relationships.

title: Asterisk Field Validation
question: Mark required fields visually and semantically while providing actionable validation messages.
answer: Use required attributes and visible labels; an asterisk alone does not explain a requirement. Include a form-level legend that defines the symbol and associate field errors with their controls. Validate normalized values so whitespace does not satisfy a required text field. Keep the server as the final authority and preserve user input on failure.
followUp: Support conditional requirements without leaving hidden fields invalid or unreachable.

title: Array.prototype.reduce
question: Reimplement reduction for array-like values with an optional initial accumulator and sparse-index semantics.
answer: Distinguish an omitted initial argument from an explicitly supplied undefined using argument count. Without an initial value, find the first present element or throw for an empty/holey input. Visit only existing indices up to the captured initial length and call the reducer with accumulator, value, index, and source. Do not add a global prototype patch in a study demo.
followUp: Compare a focused array-only implementation with the complete specification requirements for generic receivers.

title: Sidebar
question: Create a collapsible navigation sidebar that remains useful with keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
answer: Keep collapsed state separate from current-route state. Use a named nav landmark, native links, an explicit toggle button, and a visible focus indicator. If collapsed labels are hidden, preserve accessible link names. For a modal mobile drawer, make background interaction inert and restore focus when it closes; desktop navigation need not trap focus.
followUp: Persist only the layout preference and distinguish desktop collapse from mobile open state.

title: ReverseWords
question: Reverse the characters within each whitespace-delimited word while preserving word order.
answer: This contract intentionally differs from reversing the order of words. Tokenize text while preserving separator runs, reverse only word tokens by the chosen character unit, and reconstruct the original separators. Array.from handles code points but not full grapheme clusters. Keep the transformation pure so repeated calls do not mutate cached input data.
followUp: Preserve user-perceived graphemes using segmentation and compare output with reversing word order.

title: Todo List
question: Build a task list with add, complete, and delete operations using stable task IDs.
answer: Keep an array of task records and update it immutably. Trim titles before insertion and reject blanks. Generate IDs at creation, not during rendering, so editing or reordering does not attach state to a different row. Derive completed totals from records rather than synchronizing another counter. Specify whether deleting a task is immediately permanent or undoable.
followUp: Add filtered views while retaining selection and edit state by task ID.

title: Flatten Nested Objects
question: Flatten plain nested objects into path/value entries while retaining arrays as leaf values.
answer: Walk own enumerable keys, accumulate a path, and emit non-plain-object leaves. Define how empty objects and keys containing separators are represented; a segment-array path avoids dot-key ambiguity. Treat arrays as leaves for this contract rather than accidentally turning them into numeric object fields. Detect cycles along the active path and do not modify the input.
followUp: Add an inverse unflatten operation and demonstrate why ambiguous separator encoding prevents a reliable round trip.

title: Flatten Deep Object
question: Flatten a JSON-like object/array graph into unambiguous segment-array paths and leaf values.
answer: Use explicit node-type handling: arrays contribute index segments, objects contribute own key segments, and primitives become leaves. Store paths as arrays or use a reversible escaping scheme. Preserve empty containers with tagged entries if reconstructability is required. An iterative traversal avoids stack overflow, while ancestry tracking distinguishes cycles from harmless repeated references.
followUp: Preserve aliasing as reference records and explain why a tree-shaped path list otherwise loses graph identity.

title: Compress String with Limited Repetition
question: Run-length encode text while limiting each emitted run to at most k equal characters.
answer: Scan a maximal equal-character run, then split its count into chunks no larger than the positive integer cap. Emit a documented unambiguous token format rather than concatenating counts and arbitrary input characters without escaping. Keep character-unit semantics explicit and reject nonpositive caps before the loop. Work is linear in input plus emitted output.
followUp: Add a decoder and verify round trips for characters that resemble count delimiters.

title: Todo List II
question: Extend tasks with inline editing, status filters, and resilient local persistence.
answer: Use task IDs for the collection and a separate editing ID/draft for an active edit. Commit or cancel deliberately instead of mutating the saved title on each keystroke. Persist a versioned data schema and recover gracefully from corrupt or unavailable storage. Read storage before enabling writes, otherwise the initial empty render can overwrite existing tasks.
checks: edit while a filter hides the row.
followUp: Migrate an older storage schema and reconcile edits from two browser tabs.

title: Billing Counter
question: Build a checkout subtotal from item quantities, then apply a documented discount and tax order.
answer: Store quantities and item IDs, derive line totals, and calculate the bill from authoritative unit amounts. Use integer minor currency units where the domain permits, and specify rounding boundaries and discount stacking. Clamp quantities and reject unknown products. Rendering an amount is not permission to charge it; a payment server recomputes the final payable amount.
followUp: Add tax-inclusive pricing and define whether rounding occurs per line or for the whole invoice.

title: Resizable Split Pane
question: Create a two-pane workspace with a bounded draggable divider and a keyboard resizing alternative.
answer: Track the split as one value and clamp it against the container’s measured size and minimum pane widths. Use pointer capture for a drag so leaving the divider does not lose the interaction. A focusable separator needs orientation and value attributes plus arrow-key controls. Clean up observers/listeners and recalculate bounds when the container resizes.
followUp: Persist the ratio rather than raw pixels and restore it safely on a narrower device.

title: Kanban Board
question: Move cards between named columns while preserving order and unique ownership.
answer: Normalize cards by ID and store ordered ID lists per column, or use an equivalent explicit reducer. A move must remove the card from its source and insert it once into the target as one state transition. Keep drag presentation separate from committed order. Provide a keyboard or button-based move path instead of making drag the only interaction.
followUp: Add optimistic server persistence with version conflicts and rollback that preserves newer actions.

title: Tabs Component
question: Implement the complete keyboard behavior of an accessible tab list with linked panels.
answer: Maintain active and focused tab IDs according to a chosen manual or automatic activation model. Use roving tabindex, arrow-key movement, Home/End, aria-selected, and matching tab/panel IDs. Disabled tabs must be skipped consistently. Decide whether inactive panels retain state and ensure hidden panel controls are not reachable.
checks: focus after removing the active tab.
followUp: Support vertical orientation and dynamic tab removal while preserving an understandable focus target.

title: Drag And Drop II
question: Move multiple selected items between containers without losing their relative order.
answer: Represent selection by IDs independently of DOM positions. Build the source and destination arrays from a single snapshot and commit them atomically, removing selected IDs only once. Preserve the selected group’s original order and define same-container drop semantics. Expose an accessible move action for users who cannot perform a pointer drag.
followUp: Add reversible batch moves and a live announcement describing how many items moved.

title: Image Carousel
question: Display one image at a time with next/previous controls and explicit endpoint behavior.
answer: Keep an active index and derive the current slide from the image list. State whether navigation wraps or stops at the ends. Clamp or reconcile the index when data changes. Provide descriptive controls, meaningful alternative text, and a non-disruptive slide announcement. Optional autoplay requires cleanup, pause conditions, and reduced-motion support.
followUp: Pause autoplay on interaction/focus and resume only under an explicit user-controlled policy.

title: Rate Limiter
question: Implement a deterministic token-bucket model with injected time and explicit rejection behavior.
answer: Keep capacity, refill rate, current tokens, and the last update instant. Before each acquisition, refill by elapsed time and clamp to capacity, then deduct only when enough tokens remain. Time should be monotonic; handle a backwards clock according to the contract. An in-memory instance limits one process only, not a fleet of application servers.
followUp: Design an atomic shared-store update for multiple servers and state how fail-open versus fail-closed affects the product.

title: JSON.stringify
question: Serialize a documented JSON-compatible subset without pretending to implement every JSON.stringify feature.
answer: Handle primitives, arrays, and own enumerable object keys recursively. Escape control characters, quotes, and backslashes in strings. In a compatible subset, undefined/function/symbol object properties are omitted while array positions become null; nonfinite numbers become null, and cycles or BigInt require explicit handling. Track active ancestors rather than rejecting every repeated reference.
checks: unsupported value in object vs array
followUp: Add toJSON and replacer semantics only after documenting their ordering and error behavior.

title: Word Search
question: Determine whether a word exists in a rectangular character grid using adjacent non-reused cells.
answer: Start DFS/backtracking from each matching first character. At every step check bounds, character match, and current-path visitation; mark before exploring and unmark on return. Never reuse a cell within one candidate path, but allow it in a different starting search. For word length L, a coarse upper bound is O(rows*cols*4^L), with O(L) path depth.
followUp: Search many words with a trie to share prefixes and prune branches more effectively.

title: Topological Sort (DFS)
question: Return a topological order of a directed graph or report a cycle.
answer: Use three visitation states: unseen, active on the DFS path, and complete. An edge to an active node proves a directed cycle. Append nodes when their descendants finish, then reverse the completion list. Visit every vertex so disconnected components are included. Time and space are O(V+E), while deep graphs may require an explicit DFS stack.
followUp: Return a cycle witness and distinguish an edge to an active node from an edge to an already completed node.

title: Paginated Article Bookmark Viewer
question: Build an article browser whose bookmarks persist independently of pagination and search.
answer: Store page/query controls and bookmarked article IDs separately. Apply the documented order of filtering, sorting, and paging, then clamp the page when the result count shrinks. A hidden article may remain bookmarked. Distinguish local bookmark intent from server acknowledgement, and never use a page-local array index as article identity.
followUp: Add remote pagination with stale-response protection and explicit loading/error states.

title: Price Range Slider
question: Create minimum and maximum price controls that cannot cross and have equivalent numeric inputs.
answer: Keep one valid range and normalize each change against bounds and the other endpoint. For native range controls provide distinct names and visible values. Mirror number fields carefully: an incomplete numeric draft is not automatically a valid committed endpoint. Keep filtering derived from the normalized range and document inclusive boundaries.
followUp: Support currency-specific step sizes without floating-point drift in accepted prices.

title: Detect Cycle in an Undirected Connected Graph (DFS)
question: Detect a cycle in an undirected graph with a clearly declared simple-graph or multigraph model.
answer: In a simple graph DFS, an already visited neighbor that is not the current node’s parent indicates a cycle. To support disconnected input, start a traversal from every unseen vertex. For parallel edges, track edge IDs and skip only the incoming edge, since skipping every edge to the parent hides a two-edge multigraph cycle.
followUp: Produce the actual cycle path and explain how edge identity changes multigraph detection.

title: Transfer List
question: Move checked records between two lists while keeping checked state separate from list membership.
answer: Use stable IDs and two membership collections, plus a set of checked IDs. A transfer moves only eligible checked records, preserves order, and clears or reconciles checks according to the contract. Derive select-all and indeterminate states from actual eligible membership. Disable moves that would do nothing.
followUp: Add per-list search while defining whether Select all affects visible or all eligible records.

title: Star Rating
question: Build a keyboard-usable rating control with separate hover preview and committed rating.
answer: Store the committed rating and transient preview independently. Render a radiogroup or an equivalent fully implemented interaction pattern, not decorative clickable icons alone. Pointer exit restores the committed view. Arrow keys should move through valid options and accessible labels must identify values. Decide whether zero/unrated is allowed.
followUp: Support fractional display without pretending half-star selection follows automatically from integer radios.

title: Expense Tracker
question: Track dated expenses by category and derive totals under an explicit currency policy.
answer: Store immutable expense records with stable IDs and validated amounts. Prefer minor-unit integers for fixed-decimal currencies and derive category totals from the records. Keep edit drafts separate from committed entries. Specify how refunds or negative values behave rather than rejecting them accidentally. Date filtering should use a chosen calendar timezone.
followUp: Add multiple currencies with explicit conversion rates and avoid summing unlike monetary units.

title: Social Share
question: Offer sharing actions for a page URL with a usable fallback when native sharing is unavailable.
answer: Invoke the Web Share API from a user gesture when supported and fall back to a copyable URL or explicit provider links. Encode URL parameters separately instead of concatenating unescaped text. Treat user cancellation differently from a platform error. New-window links need a deliberate relationship policy and all icon controls need accessible names.
followUp: Add file sharing using capability checks without assuming every browser accepts the same file types.

title: Sortable List
question: Reorder a list while preserving item identity and exposing move-up/move-down controls.
answer: Represent order as IDs or immutable records and compute a new array for each move. Keep dragged position transient until commitment, and use pointer capture or a mature drag abstraction when needed. Render focusable alternative controls and restore focus to the moved item. Do not use array positions as keys while reordering stateful rows.
followUp: Virtualize a large list while keeping keyboard announcements and drag hit targets consistent.

title: Throttle
question: Limit function invocation rate with explicit leading/trailing behavior and cancel support.
answer: Track the last invocation time, pending timer, and latest receiver/arguments. A leading call may run immediately; a trailing call uses the newest suppressed arguments at the allowed boundary. Define the single-call behavior and cleanup semantics carefully so one interaction does not fire twice unexpectedly. Use an injected monotonic clock in tests instead of relying on wall-clock timing luck.
followUp: Add flush and define whether it changes the next allowed invocation deadline.

title: Word Counter
question: Count words in editable text according to a declared segmentation policy.
answer: For a whitespace-delimited exercise, trim, split on runs of whitespace, and return zero for blank text. Explain that this is not universal linguistic segmentation. For multilingual text, a locale-aware segmenter can identify word-like units more accurately. Derive counts from input and avoid running a costly parser multiple times per render.
followUp: Display both a simple whitespace count and a locale-aware count with their definitions.

title: Dice Roller
question: Roll a configurable number of dice and keep the result stable until the next roll.
answer: Validate die count and sides, then generate each result once in the roll handler rather than during rendering. Store the outcomes and derive the total. Inject the random source for deterministic tests. Use integer mapping appropriate to the random source and avoid claiming that a decorative animation proves fairness.
followUp: Replace pseudorandom rolls with a cryptographic uniform integer sampler and explain modulo bias.

title: PromiseAll With Concurrency Limit
question: Run lazy async task factories with bounded concurrency and input-order results.
answer: Promises already created may already be running, so accept factories. Maintain the next input index and a fixed number of worker loops. Each worker claims an index, awaits its factory, and writes the result into that index. On rejection, stop launching new work under a fail-fast contract; already running tasks need cooperative cancellation and may still finish.
followUp: Propagate an AbortSignal and distinguish rejecting the aggregate promise from undoing work already sent to a server.

title: Draw Circles
question: Create circles at pointer positions on a drawing surface with undo and clear behavior.
answer: Convert client coordinates to local surface coordinates using its bounding rectangle, and account for scaling if logical and CSS sizes differ. Store immutable circle records with stable IDs. Pointer events support mouse, touch, and pen through one path. A click outside the drawable area must not create invalid geometry.
followUp: Add redo and a keyboard placement mode without coupling geometry to browser viewport coordinates.

title: Grid Lights II
question: Record an activation order and replay deactivation at a fixed cadence after the grid is complete.
answer: Keep activated cell IDs and an explicit replay state. Reject duplicate activation and ignore user changes while replay is active unless interruption is a documented feature. Own one timer sequence with cleanup and advance through recorded order deterministically. Do not schedule independent closures that all capture an outdated array.
followUp: Support pause/resume and reverse replay using a single reducer-defined state machine.

title: Pin Items
question: Pin records above the ordinary list without losing their relative order or duplicating rows.
answer: Store pinned IDs separately from the underlying records. Derive the pinned and unpinned partitions, then concatenate them according to a documented ordering policy. Pinning should not mutate source data or replace stable keys. If search hides a pinned record, keep its pin intent unless the product explicitly removes it.
followUp: Synchronize pin preferences across devices with versioned updates instead of index-based writes.

title: Priority Queue
question: Implement a binary heap with push, peek, and pop under a comparator contract.
answer: Use array indices for parent and children. Push by appending and sifting up; pop by replacing the root with the last item and sifting down. Peek is O(1), insertion/removal O(log n), and bottom-up heap construction O(n). Define comparator direction and add an insertion sequence when equal priorities require FIFO stability.
followUp: Support priority updates using an index map and explain why changing an item in place breaks the heap unless it is repaired.

title: Memoization
question: Cache results of a pure function under an explicit argument-identity and eviction policy.
answer: Choose keys that match the function’s semantics. JSON.stringify is not a universal argument key because it loses values, can throw, and does not preserve object identity. A nested Map/WeakMap argument trie is one alternative. Cache presence separately from a falsey result, preserve the receiver if required, and bound long-lived caches. Async rejection needs an explicit cache-invalidation policy.
followUp: Combine memoization with LRU capacity and document whether concurrent callers share a pending promise.

title: Notification Bell
question: Build a notification disclosure with unread counts and idempotent mark-as-read actions.
answer: Keep notification identity and read state in records and derive unread count. Opening the panel and marking read are separate product choices; define them explicitly. Use a disclosure button with an accessible name that includes unread context, and preserve keyboard access inside the panel. Apply server events by stable IDs to avoid duplicated unread entries.
followUp: Add server acknowledgements so delayed read updates cannot resurrect old unread states.

title: Emoji Replacer
question: Replace a documented set of textual tokens with emoji while preserving unmatched text.
answer: Choose exact token boundaries and a deterministic mapping. Scan once or use an escaped alternation ordered to avoid partial overlapping matches. Keep input text as text, not injected HTML. If replacement is performed inside an editor, preserving selection and composition is a separate requirement; a derived preview is much simpler.
followUp: Implement an editable rich-text version and explain caret mapping across replacements.

title: Searchable Dropdown
question: Let users filter and select an option with keyboard navigation and an explicit empty state.
answer: Separate input query, highlighted option, selected value, and popup visibility. Use stable option IDs and reconcile the highlight when matches change. Follow combobox/listbox semantics with aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant as appropriate. Enter commits the highlighted eligible option, while Escape closes without an accidental value change.
followUp: Fetch suggestions asynchronously and prevent an older response from replacing newer matches.

title: Sum of Consecutive Integers
question: Count representations of a positive integer as a sum of one or more consecutive positive integers.
answer: For a sequence length k, subtract k(k-1)/2 from the target and require the remainder to be a positive multiple of k. Iterate lengths while the smallest possible sum 1+…+k does not exceed the target. This is O(sqrt n) arithmetic steps. Be explicit that zero/negative starting values are excluded; allowing them changes the answer and bounds.
followUp: Return each starting value and length, and relate the count to odd divisors under the same positivity assumptions.

title: Deep Clone Object
question: Clone a documented object graph while preserving cycles and repeated-reference relationships.
answer: Use a source-to-clone map and register each clone before traversing children, so cycles terminate and shared references remain shared. Handle supported types explicitly; arrays and plain objects are not enough for Date, Map, Set, or typed buffers. Functions, DOM nodes, accessors, and custom prototypes require declared behavior. Consider structuredClone when its supported type set matches the contract.
followUp: Preserve property descriptors and explain why copying getters can trigger side effects if implemented by reading values.

title: Grid Lights
question: Toggle cells in a configurable light grid and report the number currently active.
answer: Represent active cells by stable coordinates or IDs and derive the count. Use native buttons with accessible names and pressed states instead of unlabeled colored squares. Toggle with an immutable set update. If cells have dependencies, encode that rule separately rather than mutating the DOM directly.
followUp: Add a neighborhood-toggle puzzle and specify whether invalid cells or repeated events are ignored.

title: Debounce
question: Delay invocation until calls have been quiet for a fixed interval, retaining the latest receiver and arguments.
answer: Keep a timer handle and clear/restart it on every call. At expiry invoke with the last receiver/arguments and clear retained references. Add cancel to discard pending work and define flush if included. Leading/trailing options require explicit semantics rather than bolting on an extra immediate call. Test using fake time to avoid flaky sleeps.
followUp: Add leading/trailing options and prove that a single leading call does not accidentally trigger an unwanted trailing duplicate.

title: Pawn Moves
question: Highlight educational pawn moves on a board using a declared orientation and occupancy model.
answer: Represent squares as row/column coordinates and separate straight movement from diagonal captures. A pawn advances only into empty squares; a two-step start move requires both squares empty, and captures need an opposing piece. State that en passant, promotion, and king safety are excluded unless implemented explicitly.
followUp: Add promotion and en passant with move-history requirements rather than position alone.

title: Cinema Hall
question: Select available cinema seats and compute a local total without allowing reserved seats to be toggled.
answer: Use stable seat IDs and separate reserved inventory from local selection. Derive totals from selected available seats. A local selected state is only intent; a booking server must enforce availability atomically and expire holds. Render seat status through text/accessible labels as well as color, and provide predictable keyboard navigation for a large grid.
followUp: Design timed reservation holds with server authority and explain the race between two clients selecting the same seat.

title: Reusable Toast
question: Create a notification queue with unique IDs, dismissal, and predictable auto-close behavior.
answer: Own the queue in one provider or local controller and assign each toast its own deadline. Removing one toast must not clear unrelated timers. Use polite status announcements for ordinary messages and reserve urgent alerts for actual urgency. Pause timers if required by the product, preserve a dismiss button, and clean up timers when the controller unmounts.
followUp: Add action buttons whose focus and timeout policy do not remove content while a user is interacting.

title: Product Rating Heatmap
question: Display a product-by-rating intensity matrix with a legend and a readable empty-data state.
answer: Normalize counts using a documented global or per-row scale, since the choice changes interpretation. Validate numeric values and distinguish missing from zero. Render row/column labels and text alternatives so color is not the only information channel. Memoize expensive aggregation only after measuring; the displayed color should be derived from counts.
followUp: Switch between absolute and relative scales and explain how each can mislead comparisons.

title: Slugify a String
question: Derive a predictable lowercase URL slug from editable text using an explicit character policy.
answer: Choose Unicode preservation or transliteration deliberately. Normalize text, trim, fold case, replace allowed separator runs with a hyphen, and remove outer separators. Do not assume a slug is unique or use it as the sole stable database identity. Keep the raw title and generated preview separate when users may customize a slug.
followUp: Add reserved-word checks and server-side uniqueness without changing existing public URLs silently.

title: List Sorter
question: Sort a displayed collection by a selected field and direction without mutating its source.
answer: Store only sort configuration and derive a copied sorted array. Compare strings with a declared locale/collation rule and numbers numerically. Define null/missing-value ordering and add a stable tie-breaker such as ID. Sort indicators and accessible labels should describe the active configuration rather than inferred array order.
followUp: Move sorting to a paginated server and keep its ordering and tie-breakers consistent with cursor pagination.

title: Knight Moves
question: Show legal geometric knight destinations from a selected board square.
answer: Generate the eight relative L-shaped offsets, filter to board bounds, and exclude squares occupied by the same side. Unlike sliding pieces, intermediate occupancy does not block a knight. Keep the geometric movement exercise separate from full chess legality involving checks and king safety. Provide coordinate labels beyond visual highlights.
followUp: Use BFS to compute the minimum knight moves between two squares on an arbitrary board.

title: Spiral Matrix Pathfinder
question: Return matrix cells in clockwise spiral order without revisiting a cell.
answer: Maintain top, bottom, left, and right boundaries. Traverse the top row and right column, shrink those boundaries, then traverse the bottom row and left column only if a valid rectangle remains. These guard checks prevent duplication for a final single row or column. Time is O(rows*cols) and auxiliary boundary state is O(1), excluding output.
followUp: Return coordinates as well as values and define obstacle behavior as a separate pathfinding problem.

title: Queen Moves
question: Highlight queen rays until a blocker is reached on a coordinate board.
answer: Combine the four orthogonal and four diagonal directions. Walk outward square by square, adding empty squares, optionally adding the first opposing occupant, and then stop. Never continue through a piece or include a same-side occupied destination. Treat full king-safety checks as a separate layer from this geometric model.
followUp: Reuse a ray-generation helper for rook and bishop movement without mixing their distinct direction sets.

title: Lazy Evaluation
question: Build a lazy transformation pipeline that performs work only when consumed.
answer: Represent the pipeline as iterable adapters or generator functions for map/filter/take. Each consumer pull advances only enough upstream work to produce the next result. Do not materialize intermediate arrays if laziness is the goal. Define one-shot versus reusable sources and propagate iterator return/cleanup when a downstream consumer stops early.
followUp: Add async iterables with cancellation and bounded prefetch rather than launching every task eagerly.

title: BMI Calculator
question: Build an educational body-mass-index calculator with explicit unit conversion and invalid-input handling.
answer: Validate finite positive height and mass, convert height to metres, and compute mass divided by height squared. Keep raw fields editable and clear stale output on invalid submission. State units beside fields and explain that a numerical BMI is a limited screening calculation, not an individualized assessment or diagnosis.
followUp: Add unit-preserving conversions so switching units does not silently reinterpret the same raw number.

title: Longest Substring No Repeats
question: Find the longest contiguous substring containing no repeated symbols under a defined character unit.
answer: Use a sliding window and a map of each symbol’s most recent position. On repetition, move the left boundary to max(currentLeft,lastSeen+1), never backwards. Update the best window as the right side advances. This is O(n) time and O(alphabet) space over the chosen token sequence; UTF-16 indices and code-point indices must not be mixed.
followUp: Return the actual substring while preserving correct offsets when iterating Unicode code points.

title: Traffic Lights
question: Model a timed traffic-light demonstration as explicit states with one active timer.
answer: Represent the active light and a transition table containing the next state and duration. Schedule one timeout for the current state and cancel it on pause, state change, or unmount. Use functional transitions or a reducer to avoid stale closures. Make color labels visible; this UI demonstration is not a physical traffic-control safety system.
followUp: Introduce an all-red transition state and validate that no path activates conflicting lights.

title: Concurrency Limited Task Scheduler
question: Schedule tasks as they arrive while enforcing a maximum active count and an explicit cancellation contract.
answer: Keep a queue and active count. Starting a task consumes one slot; completion, synchronous throw, or rejection releases it in a finally path before pumping more work. Associate each queued task with its own resolve/reject pair. Cancelling queued work removes/rejects it; cancelling active work needs cooperation from the task. Queue capacity is separate from active concurrency.
followUp: Add backpressure and fairness priorities without starving old tasks indefinitely.

title: Find the Single Element in a Sorted Array
question: Find the lone value in a sorted odd-length array where every other value occurs exactly twice.
answer: Use binary search and align the midpoint to an even index. If nums[mid] equals nums[mid+1], intact pairs still occupy the left portion and the singleton lies to the right; otherwise it lies at or left of mid. Shrink until one index remains. This is O(log n) time and O(1) space under the exact sorted-pair precondition.
followUp: Explain why the parity invariant fails if counts are not exactly two or the array is not sorted.

title: Cards Carousel
question: Show a responsive window of cards with navigation that respects the number currently visible.
answer: Track a start index and derive the visible slice from item count and measured cards-per-view. The maximum start is max(0,total-visible), not total-1. Reconcile the index when the viewport or data changes. Keep card identities stable and ensure offscreen interactive elements are not accidentally reachable if the chosen implementation hides them.
followUp: Add virtualized card rendering and preserve focus when a previously visible card moves offscreen.

title: Event Emitter
question: Implement subscription, emission, and unsubscription with defined mutation-during-emit semantics.
answer: Store listeners per event and return an idempotent unsubscribe function. For emission, iterate a snapshot if listeners added or removed mid-emission should not change that emission. Decide whether one throwing listener stops later listeners or is collected/reported. A once listener should be removed before invocation to avoid reentrant double execution.
followUp: Add an async emit mode with a deliberate sequential versus parallel error policy.

title: List Format
question: Format a list into a human-readable conjunction with explicit empty, two-item, and locale behavior.
answer: For a locale-aware product, use Intl.ListFormat with the intended style and type. A teaching implementation can define a narrow English format: empty string for no items, the item for one, conjunction for two, and comma-separated prefix plus final conjunction for more. Do not claim that punctuation or word order generalizes across languages.
followUp: Offer a count-limited summary that reports remaining items without confusing formatting with truncation policy.

title: Map Async Limit
question: Apply an asynchronous mapper to inputs while preserving order and limiting in-flight mapper calls.
answer: Assign each input a fixed result index and let a bounded worker pool claim the next index. Await each mapper before the worker takes another item. A mapper may throw synchronously or reject, and both must follow the aggregate error policy. Validate the limit before starting. This bounds active work, not necessarily output memory, which remains proportional to input.
followUp: Return an async iterator for streaming output and compare input-order buffering with completion-order delivery.

title: Rock Paper Scissor
question: Create a round-based hand game with reproducible opponent choices and explicit score updates.
answer: Generate the opponent choice in the user-action handler, then derive win/draw/loss from a small outcome table. Update the score once per committed round and store history if needed. Keep round result separate from totals. Inject the random source for tests and reject unsupported choices rather than falling through to an accidental win.
followUp: Add best-of-N rounds with a terminal match state and an unambiguous restart action.

title: Undo Redo
question: Build editable state with undo/redo history and branch invalidation after a new edit.
answer: Represent past, present, and future. A new committed action pushes the old present into past and clears future. Undo moves present to future and restores the last past entry; redo performs the inverse. Avoid recording transient pointer movement unless intended, and cap history or store patches when snapshots become expensive.
followUp: Group a drag or typing burst into one undoable transaction rather than hundreds of snapshots.

title: Color Code Game
question: Create a color-matching round with one immutable target and a clear success/reset lifecycle.
answer: Generate target/options once per round and keep the answer fixed while the user interacts. Ensure distractors are distinct if uniqueness is part of the contract.
