Store selected answer and round status; do not infer correctness from DOM color serialization, which browsers may normalize. Provide non-color labels and deterministic random fixtures for testing.
followUp: Offer an accessible non-color challenge mode and define how hints affect scoring.

title: Stopwatch
question: Implement a stopwatch whose display remains accurate when timer callbacks are delayed.
answer: Use a monotonic clock for elapsed duration, storing accumulated time and the current run’s start timestamp. The interval requests redraws; it is not the source of elapsed truth. Pausing adds the difference to the accumulated duration, and resuming starts a new segment. Clean up the refresh interval and define reset behavior while running.
followUp: Add lap times and verify that background-tab throttling does not cause elapsed time to drift.

title: Rook Moves
question: Compute rook destinations using four bounded rays and occupancy rules.
answer: Walk horizontally and vertically from the origin. Add empty squares until the first blocker; include an opposing blocker as a possible capture and exclude a friendly blocker. Stop that ray either way. Keep row/column bounds explicit to prevent linear-index wraparound. Castling and king safety require additional state beyond this movement exercise.
followUp: Separate geometric destinations from legal moves after filtering for an exposed king.

title: Deep Omit
question: Return a new JSON-like structure with chosen property names omitted at every object depth.
answer: Traverse supported containers and build new ones without changing the source. Remove matching own keys on objects and recursively transform array elements rather than deleting array indices accidentally. Define whether key names or full paths are matched. Preserve repeated references/cycles only if graph support is part of the contract; otherwise reject cycles clearly.
followUp: Support path-pattern omission and explain how it differs from removing every key with the same name.

title: Shortest Distance from Source (BFS)
question: Find shortest edge-count distances from one source in an unweighted graph.
answer: Use a queue, initialize the source distance to zero, and mark vertices when enqueued so each vertex enters once. Each newly discovered neighbor has its parent distance plus one. Use a head index rather than repeated array shift to preserve linear queue behavior. BFS is O(V+E); it does not solve arbitrary weighted shortest paths.
followUp: Return parent links for path reconstruction and define deterministic tie-breaking among equally short paths.

title: Topological Sort (BFS)
question: Order a directed acyclic graph using indegrees and detect whether a cycle blocks completion.
answer: Compute each vertex’s indegree, enqueue all zero-indegree vertices, and remove them one by one while decrementing outgoing neighbors. Enqueue a neighbor exactly when its indegree becomes zero. If fewer than V vertices are emitted, the graph contains a cycle. Multiple valid orders exist; use a priority queue if a lexicographic choice is required.
followUp: Produce dependency layers for concurrent execution while preserving a separate cycle-reporting path.

title: Sum of Subarray Minimum
question: Sum the minimum element of every contiguous subarray using contribution counting.
answer: For each position count how many subarrays choose that element as their representative minimum, using distances to appropriate smaller boundaries. With duplicates, make one side strict and the other non-strict so equal minima are counted exactly once. Monotonic stacks find boundaries in O(n). If a modulus is required, preserve integer accuracy in multiplication and normalize negative remainders deliberately.
followUp: Return both minimum and maximum contribution totals and prove the asymmetric duplicate tie rule.

title: Modal In React
question: Create a reusable dialog that supports Escape, labelled content, and trigger focus restoration.
answer: Centralize modal open state and use a native dialog or a proven accessible primitive. The title provides its accessible name, background content must be inert for modal behavior, and focus must remain within the active dialog. Restore focus after close. A portal changes DOM placement, not the responsibility to handle accessibility and cleanup.
followUp: Handle stacked dialogs with explicit ownership rather than independent global key handlers.

title: Image Gallery
question: Build a thumbnail gallery with an accessible full-image viewer and broken-image handling.
answer: Keep selected image ID separate from the underlying list. Use thumbnail buttons with names and open the large image in a labelled dialog if modal viewing is intended. Preserve alternative text and handle missing sources. Reconcile selection when images are removed, and defer large-image loading without shifting the layout unexpectedly.
followUp: Add a predictable focus policy for keyboard navigation between thumbnails and the lightbox.

title: Typewriter Message
question: Reveal text progressively while supporting restart, changed input, and reduced motion.
answer: Track a visible boundary and derive the prefix from a pre-segmented character array. Own one timer and cancel it whenever the message, speed, run state, or component lifetime changes. Do not index by UTF-16 units if the contract promises whole graphemes. Avoid announcing every intermediate letter to screen readers; provide the full message appropriately.
followUp: Add pause/resume using a monotonic deadline rather than assuming each timer fires on time.

title: Generate Password
question: Generate a password from selected character classes and a validated length without using ordinary Math.random.
answer: Use a cryptographic random source and unbiased bounded sampling. If each selected class must appear, satisfy that constraint explicitly and shuffle the final characters without bias. Reject impossible configurations, such as too few positions for required classes. Keep the generated secret local and avoid logging it; a generated password still needs safe user handling.
followUp: Explain rejection sampling and why modulo reduction can bias a character distribution.

title: Tic Tac Toe
question: Implement a two-player board with legal turns, winner detection, draws, and restart.
answer: Store the board and next player, then derive winner/draw from the board. Ignore moves into occupied squares or after a terminal state. Check the finite winning-line set after each move. Keep cells as accessible buttons with coordinate/status labels. If move history is added, derive the displayed board from the chosen history step.
followUp: Add time-travel history and discard future moves when a player branches from an older board.

title: Temperature Convertor
question: Create linked temperature fields with one canonical editing source and explicit blank/invalid behavior.
answer: Store the most recently edited scale and raw value; derive the other scale through pure conversion. Two effects that write each other’s fields can cause loops and rounding drift. Preserve an incomplete draft instead of forcing every keystroke into a number. Specify formatting precision and never treat blank input as zero accidentally.
followUp: Add Kelvin with an explicit physical lower-bound policy and separate display rounding from stored precision.

title: Multiselect dropdown
question: Select multiple options from a searchable popup while retaining selected items outside the current results.
answer: Store selection by option ID and keep query/highlight state separate. Expose a properly implemented multiselect listbox or checkbox-based popup with accessible names. Search changes the view, not the selection. Define clear-all, disabled-option, and maximum-selection rules, and provide keyboard ways to add and remove selections.
followUp: Support remote option loading without discarding selected IDs that are absent from a particular response.

title: Captcha Generator
question: Build an explicitly labelled demo challenge with regeneration and case-sensitivity rules.
answer: Generate a new challenge only when requested and compare the answer using the declared normalization policy. Track attempts against the current challenge so old answers cannot satisfy a new one. Explain that client-generated CAPTCHA content is inspectable and cannot provide a real abuse boundary. A production defense requires server authority and accessible alternatives.
followUp: Design an accessible server-validated alternative rather than obscuring text more aggressively.

title: Confetti Animation
question: Trigger a short celebratory effect with bounded particle count and reliable cleanup.
answer: Create a finite particle set at the celebration boundary and animate transforms/opacity rather than layout properties. Stop and remove particles when the effect ends or the component unmounts. Cap simultaneous effects and avoid blocking the main thread with per-particle React state updates. Respect reduced-motion preferences with a simpler static acknowledgement.
followUp: Move a larger particle simulation to canvas while bounding frame work and lifetime.

title: Search Rotated Array
question: Search a strictly increasing array that was rotated once, assuming no duplicate values.
answer: Use binary search. At each step identify which half is sorted, then decide whether the target belongs inside that sorted interval; otherwise search the other half. Keep endpoint inclusivity consistent to avoid losing a target at mid or an edge. This remains O(log n) under the no-duplicates precondition; duplicates can make deciding the sorted side ambiguous.
followUp: Support duplicates and explain why worst-case runtime can degrade to linear.

title: Lucky Number
question: Create an entertainment-only number picker with a stable result until an explicit reroll.
answer: Define the range, validate any user seed inputs, and generate the result in the action handler. Keep display state deterministic between actions and inject randomness for tests. Present it as a game rather than a predictive claim. Reset result and feedback together so a previous round does not appear to describe a new input.
followUp: Offer a seeded reproducible mode and explain its predictability compared with random sampling.

title: Calculator
question: Implement a small arithmetic calculator without evaluating arbitrary input as JavaScript.
answer: Tokenize a documented grammar and parse operator precedence with a stack or parser. Alternatively model button entry as an explicit accumulator/operator state machine for a simpler calculator. Define unary minus, decimal entry, division by zero, and repeated equals behavior. Arbitrary eval is not a parser and creates both correctness and injection problems.
followUp: Add parentheses with a real grammar and separate numeric precision policy from input parsing.

title: Combination Sum
question: Return unique combinations of distinct positive candidates that sum to a target, allowing reuse.
answer: Sort validated positive candidates and backtrack from a start index. Recurse with the same index to allow reuse, and move the loop index forward to avoid permutation duplicates. Stop when the remaining target is zero and prune candidates larger than it. Zero or negative candidates would invalidate this termination argument and need a different contract.
followUp: Implement a single-use variant and explain how advancing the recursive start index changes the search space.

title: Markdown Editor
question: Show a Markdown preview while treating document content as untrusted input.
answer: Keep raw Markdown as the editing source and debounce expensive parsing only when measurements justify it. Use a supported parser and a separate sanitization policy for HTML, dangerous URL schemes, and optional raw HTML. Never pass unsanitized user HTML into the page. Preserve editor selection and expose a text-only reading path where useful.
followUp: Add asynchronous preview computation with revision checks so stale parses cannot overwrite newer text.

title: Animated Loading Skeleton
question: Represent a loading layout without treating loading placeholders as real content.
answer: Keep loading state explicit and reserve approximately the final layout dimensions to reduce shifts. Mark the affected region busy and keep decorative skeleton shapes hidden from assistive technology. Stop looping motion under reduced motion and replace loading with error or empty states when appropriate; an endless shimmer must not hide a failed request.
followUp: Coordinate several regions so partial data can render without resetting already usable sections.

title: Implement Promise Race
question: Create an aggregate promise that adopts the first settlement from an iterable of values or promises.
answer: Return a promise and attach fulfillment/rejection handlers through Promise.resolve for each iterable item. The first resolve/reject wins naturally through promise settlement rules; later settlements are ignored. An empty iterable leaves the result pending. Iteration errors must reject the aggregate. This is a focused implementation model, not a full recreation of subclass and species behavior.
followUp: Contrast race with any and explain why winning a race does not cancel losing operations.

title: Auto Save Form
question: Persist a multi-field form with debouncing, revision-aware acknowledgements, and conflict feedback.
answer: Track a draft revision and the last acknowledged snapshot. Send only an intended snapshot, and ignore acknowledgements that refer to an older revision when displaying saved status. Cancel idle timers on edit/unmount, but do not assume cancelling a client request undoes a server write. Server version checks are needed to prevent late writes from overwriting newer persisted state.
followUp: Use optimistic concurrency with a document version and an explicit user merge workflow.

title: Drag and Drop
question: Reorder a small list through pointer dragging while retaining a non-drag alternative.
answer: Separate the dragged item ID and hover target from the committed order. On drop compute one immutable reorder and clear transient state; on cancellation restore the original arrangement. Use stable keys and ensure event listeners or pointer capture are released. Provide move buttons or a complete keyboard drag model instead of assuming pointer input.
followUp: Announce drag start, destination, and completion through a restrained live region.

title: Progress Bar II
question: Run several queued progress tasks with explicit capacity and completion behavior.
answer: Model each task as queued, running, completed, failed, or cancelled. Start no more than the allowed active count and release capacity on every terminal path. Derive progress from completed work or elapsed simulation time according to the contract. Keep timers/controllers keyed by task ID and clean them up when tasks disappear.
followUp: Replace simulated time with real byte/work acknowledgements and keep retry progress semantics explicit.

title: JSON Formatter and Validator
question: Validate JSON text and show formatted output without losing the original invalid draft.
answer: Parse using JSON.parse inside try/catch and derive formatted output only after successful parsing. Show a useful error region and clear stale formatted output when the input becomes invalid. Bound input size for a UI utility and do not run large blocking work on every keystroke. JSON is a data format, not arbitrary JavaScript object syntax.
followUp: Move large-document parsing to a Worker and discard stale parse results by revision.

title: Quiz App
question: Build a question-by-question quiz whose answers, progress, and final score have one clear source of truth.
answer: Use stable question IDs and store answers by ID. Derive answered count and score from those answers and the authored scoring rule. Prevent accidental double submission and define whether users may revise previous answers. Model in-progress and completed states explicitly, and make result feedback accessible without forcing unexpected focus changes.
followUp: Support multiple correct answers with a documented partial-credit policy and reproducible question order.

title: Reverse Words in a String
question: Reverse the order of whitespace-delimited words and normalize separators to single spaces.
answer: Trim the input, split on runs of whitespace, reverse the token sequence, and join with one space. This contract intentionally normalizes spacing and leaves the letters inside each word unchanged. Guard empty input so it produces an empty string. A preserve-original-whitespace variant is a different specification and should not be inferred from the same function name.
followUp: Implement a separator-preserving variant and define precisely which separator attaches to which word after reversal.

title: Oranges Rotting
question: Compute the minimum simultaneous spread steps in a grid or report unreachable fresh cells.
answer: Start a multi-source BFS with every initially active source and count remaining susceptible cells. Each level represents one unit of time; mark cells when enqueued so they are not counted twice. If the queue empties with susceptible cells remaining, report failure. Keep the all-already-complete case at zero and decide whether the input grid may be mutated.
followUp: Return the activation time of every cell and preserve the original grid by storing visitation separately.

title: Object.assign()
question: Copy own enumerable string and symbol properties from sources into a target with explicit shallow-copy semantics.
answer: Convert a non-null target to an object and skip null/undefined sources. Enumerate each source’s own enumerable keys, including symbols, and assign values in source order so later sources overwrite earlier ones. This reads getters and invokes target setters; it does not copy descriptors or recursively clone children. Throwing accessors can leave a partially changed target.
followUp: Compare assignment semantics with descriptor copying and immutable object spread without claiming they are identical.

title: Merge Array
question: Merge two sorted numeric arrays into a new sorted array in linear time.
answer: Use one pointer per input and repeatedly append the smaller current value, then append either remainder. This is O(n+m) time and O(n+m) output space. Decide whether equal values are all retained; a merge is not automatically a deduplication operation. Do not sort the combined data when sorted inputs already provide the needed structure.
checks: all of one array precedes the other
followUp: Merge k sorted streams with a heap and discuss finite arrays versus unbounded iterators.

title: pyramid pattern
question: Produce a centered text pyramid for a validated nonnegative row count.
answer: For row i starting at zero, emit height-i-1 leading spaces and 2*i+1 fill symbols under a one-column-symbol contract. Return joined lines rather than mixing generation with console output. The output itself has O(height squared) size, so that cost cannot be optimized away if the full pyramid is required. Define trailing-space and final-newline behavior explicitly.
followUp: Support a hollow pyramid and define how multi-column Unicode symbols affect visual alignment.

title: Search in a 2D Sorted Matrix
question: Search a matrix whose rows and columns are nondecreasing, without assuming row ranges do not overlap.
answer: Start at the top-right cell. If the target is smaller, move left; if larger, move down. Each comparison discards one row or column, yielding O(rows+cols) time and O(1) extra space. Flattened binary search is only valid under the stronger property that every row starts after the previous row ends.
followUp: Compare the staircase algorithm with flattened binary search and state their different preconditions.

title: King Moves
question: Highlight adjacent king destinations while distinguishing geometry from complete chess legality.
answer: Generate the eight neighboring offsets and discard out-of-bounds or same-side occupied targets. These are geometric destinations only: a real king also cannot move into attack. Attack-map calculation, castling rights, and full board legality belong in a separate rule layer rather than being implied by the highlighted squares.
followUp: Add an opponent attack map and verify that king moves cannot enter check.

title: Detect data type in JS
question: Classify JavaScript values using a declared category model rather than assuming typeof is complete.
answer: Use explicit checks for null and Array.isArray before typeof-based primitive handling. Add supported built-ins deliberately; Object.prototype.toString can help with cross-realm values but Symbol.toStringTag may spoof its label. Avoid instance-of-only checks across realms. A type inspector should report its confidence/contract rather than treating display labels as a security boundary.
followUp: Separate semantic validation of a value from a convenience diagnostic type label.

title: Bishop Moves
question: Compute diagonal bishop rays that stop at the first occupied square.
answer: Walk in the four diagonal directions with explicit row/column bounds. Empty squares are reachable; the first opposing occupant can be included as a capture, while a friendly occupant cannot. Stop after either type of blocker. Reuse traversal mechanics without confusing this geometric result with legal moves under king safety.
followUp: Integrate the ray model into an attack-map calculation that handles pinned pieces deliberately.

title: Pagination
question: Design a data browser whose page, filters, sort, total count, and browser history remain consistent.
answer: Choose offset or cursor semantics before building controls. For offset paging, apply filters/sort before slicing and clamp the current page after totals change. For cursor paging, preserve server cursors and avoid inventing random page access. Key requests by the complete query configuration and reject stale responses. Loading a new page should not erase already usable navigation unnecessarily.
followUp: Compare offset and keyset pagination under concurrent inserts using a stable unique tie-breaker.

title: Nested Checkbox
question: Implement a hierarchy where a parent checkbox reflects all descendant leaf selections.
answer: Store selected leaves or an equivalent normalized model. Derive a parent’s checked and indeterminate states from descendant coverage; indeterminate is a DOM property, not merely an attribute. Parent activation applies a documented action to all eligible descendants. Keep IDs unique and define disabled-subtree behavior explicitly. Avoid storing contradictory parent and child booleans independently.
followUp: Support lazy-loaded children without incorrectly declaring an incompletely known subtree fully selected.

title: File Explorer
question: Build a file tree with expand/collapse, selection, create, rename, and delete operations.
answer: Use stable node IDs, parent relationships, and a separate ordered-child representation or an immutable nested reducer. Validate sibling names and prevent moving a directory into itself or a descendant. Keep expanded/selected/editing state outside display labels. Use either a fully implemented tree keyboard pattern or semantic nested disclosures. Reconcile selection and focus after deletion.
followUp: Add optimistic server operations with version conflicts and reversible mutations.

title: Prim's MST Algorithm
question: Construct a minimum spanning tree for a connected, weighted, undirected graph.
answer: Grow a visited set from one start vertex. Push boundary edges into a minimum heap, repeatedly choose the cheapest edge entering an unvisited vertex, and add that vertex’s outgoing edges. Skip edges whose destination is already visited. A lazy heap implementation is O(E log E), often expressed as O(E log V) for ordinary simple graphs. Negative edge weights are allowed; connectivity must be checked.
followUp: Return a minimum spanning forest for disconnected input and explain why directed graphs need a different problem formulation.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
question: Find the longest contiguous balanced-parentheses substring in a parentheses-only string.
answer: Use a stack of indices seeded with -1 as the boundary before a candidate segment. Push opening indices; on a closing symbol pop, then either reset the boundary if the stack is empty or measure the span from the current index to the stack top. This is O(n) time and O(n) worst-case stack space. The goal is a substring, not a subsequence.
followUp: Compare the stack solution with a two-pass counter method and explain why both directions are needed there.

title: StickyNotes Component
question: Create draggable notes with editable text, stacking order, deletion, and persisted positions.
answer: Store stable note IDs, content, and logical positions. During pointer movement update presentation efficiently and commit a bounded position on release. Keep editing gestures separate from dragging, and define a z-order policy. Persist a versioned schema and recover corrupt storage. Provide a keyboard position alternative and account for container resize rather than restoring offscreen pixel coordinates blindly.
followUp: Add shared-board synchronization with explicit conflict resolution for concurrent text and position edits.

title: Chinese Remainder Theorem
question: Solve simultaneous congruences with positive pairwise-coprime moduli using exact integer arithmetic.
answer: Let M be the product of moduli and Mi=M/mi. Compute the modular inverse of Mi modulo mi using the extended Euclidean algorithm, then sum ai*Mi*inverse and normalize modulo M. Use BigInt so intermediate products remain exact. If moduli are not pairwise coprime, the inverse-based formula is invalid; a generalized merge must test residue compatibility modulo each gcd.
followUp: Implement generalized pairwise merging and return no solution when the residue difference is not divisible by the gcd.

title: 24 Game
question: Build a puzzle where each of four supplied numbers is used exactly once to produce 24 with arithmetic operators.
answer: For a solver, recursively choose two current values, combine them with each allowed operation, and recurse on the reduced multiset. Keep the expression tree alongside each result and avoid division by zero. Use rational arithmetic for exactness or a documented tolerance for floating-point comparison. The input UI needs its own grammar if users type expressions; do not use eval.
followUp: Use exact rational pairs and canonical-state memoization to avoid repeating symmetric search branches.

title: OTP Input Component
question: Implement a multi-slot verification-code field with paste, editing, focus movement, and accessible labels.
answer: Decide whether to use one semantic input with visual slots or multiple coordinated inputs. Keep one canonical code string, normalize permitted characters, and handle paste as a batch update. Define Backspace behavior and focus movement without fighting IME composition or assistive technology. Autofill support and error announcement require real browser testing. Verification and rate limiting remain server responsibilities.
followUp: Add an expiry/resend flow that does not let an old code submission overwrite a newer challenge state.

title: Event Management
question: Manage scheduled events with date/time editing, overlap rules, and a clearly chosen timezone.
answer: Store stable event IDs and distinguish instants from local calendar entries. Define overlap boundaries, such as half-open intervals, before checking conflicts. Parse and validate user fields explicitly, including end after start. Keep editing drafts separate from saved events. Recurring events and daylight-saving transitions cannot be handled reliably by adding fixed milliseconds to local dates.
followUp: Add recurrence with a timezone-aware rule model and define how exceptions and rescheduling are represented.

title: Tree Navigation
question: Create keyboard-navigable hierarchical content with a predictable active and focused node.
answer: Separate expansion, selection, and keyboard focus. If implementing an ARIA tree, use roving tabindex and the expected arrow/Home/End rules, including moving to a parent or first child. Stable IDs let expansion survive reordering. For a simple document outline, ordinary nested links may be more appropriate than a tree widget. Lazy loading needs an explicit busy/error state.
followUp: Virtualize a large tree while keeping the visible keyboard order and accessibility relationships correct.

title: Product Cart with Discounts
question: Compute an editable cart total under an explicit discount stacking and rounding contract.
answer: Normalize products and cart quantities by ID. Derive a pricing pipeline with a documented order for line discounts, order discounts, tax, and shipping. Use appropriate monetary arithmetic and ensure discounts cannot create negative payable amounts unless credits are part of the model. Client totals are estimates: the server validates prices, coupons, inventory, and final payable amounts.
followUp: Design a server quote/version mechanism so payment uses the exact accepted pricing snapshot.

title: Data Table
question: Build an accessible sortable/filterable table with selection, pagination, and stable row identity.
answer: Keep query controls and selected row IDs separate from the dataset. Define whether transformations occur locally or on the server and apply a consistent ordering pipeline. Native table markup preserves row/column relationships; sortable headers expose aria-sort. Selection across pages must use stable IDs and an explicit select-all scope. Virtualization, editing, and grids add interaction complexity beyond a plain table.
followUp: Support server-side select-all as a query plus exclusions rather than downloading every row ID.

title: Match Pair Game
question: Create a memory game that reveals two cards, locks during mismatch resolution, and supports restart.
answer: Represent cards by stable pair IDs and card-instance IDs. Track revealed unmatched cards, permanently matched pairs, and an explicit resolving state. Ignore clicks on a matched/already revealed card and block a third reveal during the delay. Clear the mismatch timer on restart or unmount so an old round cannot modify the new board. Inject shuffle randomness for tests.
followUp: Add a reduced-motion mode and an accessible announcement strategy that preserves the puzzle’s rules.

title: Kruskal's MST Algorithm
question: Build a minimum spanning forest by selecting sorted edges that connect different components.
answer: Sort undirected edges by weight, then use a disjoint-set union structure with path compression and union by rank/size. Accept an edge only if its endpoints have different representatives, then union those components. Sorting dominates at O(E log E); DSU operations are almost constant amortized. A connected graph’s result has V-1 edges; disconnected input produces a forest unless the contract rejects it.
followUp: Return component information and a deterministic tie-breaking policy without claiming the MST is unique.

title: Implement LRUCache
question: Implement a fixed-capacity cache with O(1) average get/put and explicit recency updates.
answer: Combine a key-to-node map with a doubly linked list, moving accessed/updated nodes to the most-recent end and evicting the least-recent node at capacity. A JavaScript Map can model insertion-order recency by delete-and-set under an average-time contract. Distinguish missing keys from cached undefined and define zero-capacity behavior. Updating an existing key must not increase size.
followUp: Add TTL expiration and explain why recency, expiration, and capacity are independent policies.

title: Nested Comments
question: Build a threaded comment model with replies, editing, deletion, and stable nesting relationships.
answer: Normalize comments by ID with parent IDs and ordered child lists, or use a carefully immutable tree. Keep editing drafts local to the chosen ID and avoid recursive index keys. Define deletion as subtree removal or a tombstone that preserves replies. Sanitize any supported rich content and derive displayed authors from trusted server records. Deep threads need bounded rendering and accessible reply context.
followUp: Add optimistic replies with temporary IDs and reconcile server acknowledgements without duplicating the thread.

title: Implement a Queue using Stack
question: Provide FIFO enqueue/dequeue/peek using two LIFO stacks.
answer: Push new values onto an incoming stack. When the outgoing stack is empty, transfer every incoming value to it, reversing order once; then pop or peek outgoing. Each item moves at most once between stacks, giving amortized O(1) operations although one transfer costs O(n). Define underflow separately from a stored undefined value.
followUp: Explain amortized analysis using a potential function and contrast it with worst-case per-operation latency.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
question: Find the median of two sorted arrays without merging their full contents.
answer: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array and derive the corresponding partition in the other so the left side contains half the combined elements. A valid partition has both left maxima no greater than the opposite right minima. The median is the left maximum for odd total length, or the average of the two central values for even length. Use sentinels at empty sides and reject two empty inputs.
followUp: Return the kth element through a related partition argument and address overflow-safe averaging in fixed-width arithmetic.

title: Rick And Morty Characters Viewer
question: Create a character-directory UI with query filters, paginated fetching, and resilient request state.
answer: Treat the external API as a replaceable data source with a documented response adapter. Key requests by search/filter/page, cancel or ignore stale responses, and distinguish loading, no matches, unavailable service, and malformed data. Do not assume a sample API is always online or that page totals stay stable. Preserve user controls and give errors a retry action.
followUp: Add a cache with explicit freshness rules and avoid replaying cached data from a different query.

title: Product Store
question: Build a store browsing flow with catalog queries, product details, cart intent, and resilient navigation.
answer: Separate remote product data from local query and cart state. Use stable product IDs and validate stale or missing products. Keep prices authoritative on the server and treat local cart totals as previews. A complete commerce system also needs checkout, stock reservation, idempotent payment, and recovery; browsing components alone do not provide those guarantees.
followUp: Trace a checkout across quote creation, inventory hold, payment confirmation, and retry-safe order creation.

title: Create Task Scheduler With Dependencies
question: Execute a dependency DAG with bounded concurrency and explicit failure propagation.
answer: Validate task IDs and dependency references, compute indegrees, and queue initially ready tasks. Completion releases dependents by decrementing their unresolved dependency count. Define whether a failed task blocks descendants, triggers cancellation, or allows a compensating policy. Detect cycles independently so an empty ready queue is not mistaken for successful completion. Concurrency slots must be released on every settlement.
followUp: Persist task states for restart recovery and distinguish at-least-once execution from idempotent task effects.

title: All Pairs Shortest Path (Floyd-Warshall Algorithm)
question: Compute weighted shortest distances between every vertex pair and detect negative cycles.
answer: Initialize diagonal distances to zero and each direct edge to the minimum parallel-edge weight. For each intermediate vertex k, relax every i,j through k, keeping k as the outer loop. Skip unreachable additions. Runtime is O(V cubed) and storage O(V squared). A negative diagonal indicates a negative cycle; pairs that can route through it do not have a finite shortest distance.
followUp: Maintain a next-hop matrix for path reconstruction and mark pairs whose result is unbounded by a reachable negative cycle.

title: Shortest Distance from Source (Bellman-Ford Algorithm)
question: Find single-source shortest paths with negative edges and identify reachable negative cycles.
answer: Initialize the source to zero and other distances to infinity. Relax all edges up to V-1 passes, stopping early if no distance changes. An additional successful relaxation from a reachable vertex proves a reachable negative cycle. A negative cycle in an unreachable component does not invalidate source distances. Runtime is O(VE), with O(V) distance storage.
followUp: Propagate an unbounded marker to every vertex reachable from a detected negative cycle.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
question: Return the maximum for each fixed-width contiguous window in linear time.
answer: Maintain a deque of candidate indices in decreasing value order. Remove indices that have left the window from the front and dominated candidates from the back before adding the new index. The front is the current maximum. Each index enters and leaves at most once, yielding O(n) time and O(k) auxiliary space. Use a head pointer or real deque rather than repeated shift.
followUp: Return maximum positions with a documented oldest-versus-newest tie policy for equal values.

title: Worker Pool
question: Distribute CPU tasks across a bounded pool of actual Workers with task IDs and failure handling.
answer: A promise concurrency loop does not create CPU parallelism. Create a limited number of Workers, send serializable tasks, and correlate results by unique IDs. Release or replace a worker on success, failure, or timeout and settle each task exactly once. Structured cloning and transferables affect cost and ownership. Cancellation may require terminating a worker and rebuilding its state.
followUp: Add backpressure, per-task deadlines, and worker replacement without leaking unsettled promises.

title: First Missing Positive
question: Find the smallest absent positive integer in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space when mutation is allowed.
answer: For length n, the answer lies between 1 and n+1. Repeatedly place each in-range integer x into position x-1, stopping when it is already in the right place or a duplicate would make swapping loop. Then scan for the first index whose value is not index+1. State that this mutates the input; a nonmutating Set version has a different space contract.
followUp: Prove that each successful placement makes progress and contrast the mutation contract with a pure implementation.

title: Design Autocomplete
question: Design prefix suggestions with ranking, bounded results, updates, and explicit query semantics.
answer: For a static prefix dictionary, a trie or sorted-array prefix range can locate candidates. Ranking may require cached top-k entries per prefix or a separate scoring index. Define case/Unicode normalization, ties, and update behavior before selecting a structure. Client debouncing does not solve server ranking, authorization, privacy, or cache freshness; protect against stale suggestion responses separately.
followUp: Compare trie top-k caches with a search index when ranking depends on user context and rapidly changing popularity.

title: Shortest Distance from Source (Dijkstra's Algorithm)
question: Compute shortest paths from one source in a graph with nonnegative edge weights.
answer: Use a min-heap of candidate distances, initialize the source to zero, and relax outgoing edges from the smallest valid entry. With a lazy heap, skip entries whose recorded distance is stale. Reject negative weights because the settled-distance argument no longer holds. Complexity with a binary heap is typically O((V+E) log V), with implementation-dependent lazy-heap bounds.
followUp: Add path reconstruction and compare with Bellman–Ford when negative weights are permitted.

title: Fibonacci Modulo (Pisano Period)
question: Compute a very large Fibonacci index modulo m using a clearly bounded number-theory strategy.
answer: A Pisano period is the repetition length of the pair (F_n mod m,F_(n+1) mod m). For small moduli, detect the return to (0,1), reduce n by the period, and compute the reduced term. Handle m=1 separately. Period discovery may be too expensive for large moduli; fast doubling computes F_n mod m in O(log n) arithmetic steps without discovering a period.
followUp: Use fast doubling as the general method and explain when explicit period discovery is useful or wasteful.

title: Implement Garbage Collector
question: Simulate mark-and-sweep collection on an explicit heap graph rather than attempting to control JavaScript memory.
answer: Represent heap objects as IDs with outgoing references and provide an explicit root set. Mark every reachable object using a visited traversal, then sweep only unmarked allocated objects. Unreachable cycles are collected because reachability is defined from roots, not incoming-reference count alone. This model excludes real engine barriers, generations, moving collectors, finalizers, and concurrent mutation.
followUp: Add an incremental marking model and state the write-barrier invariant needed when the graph changes during marking.
